metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.candidate_universe: Evidence collected across two predeclared production domains for symmetry with other languages: (1) primary/client application domain evidence (the domain the language was designed for), and (2) a secondary/expansion domain (server-side), each backed by named organizations or an externally observable aggregator, collected via the same retrieval route and depth as other assigned languages.

component_findings.current_continuity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): Indicates Swift usage is concentrated (Apple-platform specialist niche) rather than broad general-purpose usage, which is a limitation on the breadth (though not depth) of production evidence.
component_findings.deployment_depth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): Swift has overwhelming, unambiguous production deployment evidence as the dominant language for the entire Apple first-party and third-party app ecosystem (iOS/macOS/watchOS/tvOS), including Apple's own products. This is an extremely large-scale, verifiable production footprint. Secondary-domain (server-side) production evidence exists (Vapor/SwiftNIO, documented company migrations) but is comparatively narrower and includes a documented high-profile framework abandonment (IBM Kitura), and overall developer population using Swift day-to-day is a small share of all professional developers. The score reflects very strong depth of production adoption in its core domain offset by narrower breadt

metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: Declared as a breadth proxy from a commercial technology-detection aggregator; not verified per-company and used only alongside named case evidence, not standalone.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.candidate_universe: For each tool category (IDE/editor integration, LSP, formatter, linter, debugger, package manager, version manager, CI/CD packaging), select the tool that is either (a) officially shipped/maintained by Apple/swiftlang, or (b) the de-facto community-standard tool most commonly referenced in official Swift.org documentation and package ecosystem write-ups. Candidate universe considered: Xcode, sourcekit-lsp, swift-format, SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, LLDB, SwiftPM, CocoaPods, Carthage, swiftly, Mint, Swift Package Index, VS Code Swift extension, swift.nvim.

component_findings.build_test_coverage: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): Swift has a complete, largely first-party tool chain (IDE, LSP, formatter, linter, debugger, package manager, version manager) plus a mature, Apple-backed package discovery service and widely-adopted third-party quality tools (SwiftLint, SwiftFormat). This is comparable to top-tier ecosystems, but cross-platform (non-Apple OS) tooling maturity and editor-agnostic experience lag slightly behind languages designed cross-platform from inception, justifying a strong but not maximal score.
component_findings.ci_devops: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): Third-party package managers (Mint, Tuist): Mint adds 1.8 s overhead per mint run invocation due to SwiftPM wrapper layering.
component_findings.debug_profile: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): First-party Apple IDE with integrated build, debug, profiling (Instruments), and SwiftUI preview tooling; the default and dominant development environment for Swift on Apple platforms.
component_findings.editor_ide: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): Swift has a complete, largely first-party tool chain (IDE, LSP, formatter, linter, debugger, package manager, version manager) plus a mature, Apple-backed package discovery service and widely-adopted third-party quality tools (SwiftLint, SwiftFormat). This is comparable to top-tier ecosystems, but cross-platform (non-Apple OS) tooling maturity and editor-agnostic experience lag slightly behind languages designed cross-platform from inception, justifying a strong but not maximal score.
component_findings.lint_format_static: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--swift): A comprehensive, modular Neovim plugin for Swift development with LSP, build tools, formatting, linting, and integrated LLDB debugger

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Tooling is heavily macOS/Xcode-centric; Linux and other-platform tooling (VS Code + sourcekit-lsp, Docker toolchains) exists but is documented as secondary/rougher, e.g. higher cold-start latency and extra RAM for non-Xcode setups per one technical comparison. | Raw GitHub star counts (e.g. SwiftLint's ~12.9K stars) are used only as a declared, consistently-collected proxy alongside qualitative adoption evidence, not as a standalone score. | SourceKit-LSP itself notes ongoing rough edges: 'SourceKit-LSP is still in early development, so you may run into rough edges with any of the features.'
metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
